newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwean shares weaken on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwean shares weaken on profit-taking.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares weakened amidst some profit-taking on Wednesday but brokers said they expected the market to maintain a firm undertone for the rest of the week underpinned by high liquidity which has seen it reach record levels in the past few days.
The main industrial index shed 23.02 points to end at 12,058.93.
"The sentiment on the market was that it had become a bit overvalued but there's still lots of money out there so the firm undertone should remain," one broker said.

"There's some profit-taking, it could be that people are trying to get money to get into CBZ (the Commercial Bank of Zimbabwe)," he added in reference to the launch earlier on Wednesday of the government's sale of 80 percent of its stake in CBZ.

On the bourse on Wednesday, merchant banker FMB leapt 200 cents to 4,800, tobacco firm BAT jumped 100 cents to 1,600, agricultural firm Acacia rose 50 cents to 300, clothing retailer Edgars gained 20 cents to 800 and publisher Zimpapers added five cents to 165.
Among the day's losers, merchant banker NMB at 3,550, timber producer Border at 3,550 and food group Natfoods at 900 all dropped 50 cents while banker Barclays shed 25 cents to 3,300.
Minings were active and firmer with Wankie Colliery trading 25 cents up at 850 and gold producer Rio Tinto rose 100 cents to 1,600 but Ashanti slid 1,000 cents to 8,000.
The mining index rose 18.68 points to end at 898.17.
